questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University's academic reputation in my line of studies, the courses offered, the student environment and the nature in the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall good, the only con is that the student housing was really delayed in their answers, i did'nt know if i had a place to live before less than a week before arriving.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All the information got to me and was fairlyb easy to find, but there was so much that i could not manage o read it all, so a prioritization in importance of the information would have been nice, so i knew what to prioritise.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned an academic cohort leader for academic questions and a visiting student person for personal or general questions, and though i did not really use it, it was really nice having the opppertunity and knowing who to contact.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: One could apply through the uni with a prioritised list with up to 5 priorities. I did not get any of those housing, but under a week before i was offered somethin else, which was more expensive, but had to say yes to, because the process got dragged out for so long, that i could not find anything else.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Yes, there was a kitchen, but no kitchenware, so i has to go and by everything - plates, pots, pans, kitchen utensisls, baking trays, knivesm cutlery and so on.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That they are really delayed, so it would probably be better to find somethin yourself if you want to be sure that you have housing, and that it is usually pretty expensive through uni. Furthermore you should jnow that it helps to call them and ask for them to help - call every day multiple times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine, but too expensive and the answers were too delayed.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you have arrived you have to go to international student check in on campus, where you have to provide a list of documents. That is the only registration from the host institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I guess one could have asked the visiting student office if one was in doubt.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy to get the courses i wanted - although it should be noted that none of them were 'high-demand popular courses' or outside my academic experience. I also changed one course in the drop-period, and that worked well too.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as it opens, and change them as soon as you know you want to. Then you will probably get all the courses you wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes were great - they were interesting and all had really engaged professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses that fit with my own, and the level was perfect - interesting and chellenging, but not too hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar in teaching style and how the courses were conducted. Although, it was different in terms of assesment, where i was graded throughout the semester and did not have an exam period without teaching to prepare, so this was a little stressful as it was different and one definitely has to readjust.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Fieldwork Approaches for the Study of Religion (DIVI10038), Regional Perspectives in a Globalised Muslim World (10107) and Science, Sorcery and Wonder in Islam(DIVI10108)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All three of them - great professors and really interesting topics; Fieldwork Approaches for the Study of Religion (DIVI10038), Regional Perspectives in a Globalised Muslim World (10107) and Science, Sorcery and Wonder in Islam(DIVI10108)

questions.answer: Nothing unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I had researched on prices in advance, so no surprises there

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offered great things, but i did not have time, though friends really enjoyed the different clubs

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hundreds of associations - everything from dance, to painting to foraging to rugby.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not go, but everyone recommends the hillwalking club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to isle of skye, up the east coast, to cairngorms, glasgow - in general just explore. Flixbus drives between cities, and there is also trains. You can also rent a car, which i did a couple of times.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine, it is not that different from what i am used to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is a little difficult with local students, i think mainly talk to those you have classes with and join a club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any of them particularaly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendlines - people are really nice!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find your accomodation yourself, take courses in a similar level as you are at home, and take some trips out of the city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot of new things in class and seeing the beautiful country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing was the biggest challenge - expensive, late answers and non-social roommates.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
